name: Quantitative Common-Section Gluing Bound
statement: For common-section pieces $A_i$ over $D$, let $h_i=\max_{a\in A_i}d_H(a,D)$, $\kappa_i=\max\{h_i-1,0\}$, and let $\kappa_{(2)}$ be the second largest $\kappa_i$ with multiplicity, or zero for one piece. Then $\max_i\sigma(A_i)\leq\sigma(X)\leq\max\{\max_i\sigma(A_i),\kappa_{(2)}\}$. If all but at most one piece have $h_i\leq1$, equality holds with the maximum piece width.
proof: Every piece is a conditioning of the union, giving the lower bound. Order a piece with largest $\kappa_i$ first, then append the outside concepts of each other piece after the base $D$. The gate of a current concept into $D$ has disagreement contained in every cross-piece disagreement, so cross-piece predecessors add no new minimal supports. Each appended piece costs at most the maximum of its absolute width and $\kappa_i$, leaving only the second largest attachment penalty.
